items.title: [Bug]: [CUDA] cute::make_int_sequence<cute::size(...)> fails in dependent template contexts

labels.name: Windows
labels.description: <NV>Windows operating system specific issues and compatibility problems

labels.name: Customized kernels
labels.description: <NV>Specialized/modified CUDA kernels in TRTLLM for LLM ops, beyond standard TRT. Dev & perf.

items.body:
### System Info

- Discovered on Windows Server 2025 with MSVC as the NVCC host compiler
- Visual Studio Build Tools with MSVC 19.51.36248
- MSVC toolset 14.51.36231
- CUDA/NVCC 13.2, V13.2.51
- C++20
- `--gpu-architecture=sm_89`
- `--expt-relaxed-constexpr`
- `--expt-extended-lambda`
- `/Zc:preprocessor`
- CuTe from the CUTLASS dependency vendored with FlashInfer
- CUTLASS revision `e6e2cc29`
- The reproduced diagnostic is emitted by NVCC during dependent-template instantiation
- The defect does not appear to be specific to Windows or MSVC

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [ ] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [ ] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

### Background

Hi!

I encountered this issue on Windows while building SystemPanic/vllm-windows for a DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 deployment. The affected FP8 blockscale GEMM kernel originates from TensorRT-LLM and is vendored through FlashInfer, so I am reporting the issue here in the hope that the portable source fix can be incorporated upstream. Although the failure was reproduced with NVCC 13.2 using MSVC as the host compiler, the diagnostic occurs during NVCC dependent-template instantiation and may not be Windows-specific.

The affected TensorRT-LLM source file is:

```text
cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/cutlass_kernels/fp8_blockscale_gemm/ada_blockwise_gemm/sm89_fp8_gemm_1d1d.cuh
```

The corresponding vendored FlashInfer path is:

```text
csrc/nv_internal/tensorrt_llm/kernels/cutlass_kernels/fp8_blockscale_gemm/ada_blockwise_gemm/sm89_fp8_gemm_1d1d.cuh
```

The issue was reproduced with CUDA/NVCC 13.2 using MSVC as the host compiler. The diagnostic is emitted during NVCC dependent-template instantiation. 

The affected SM89 kernel passes the CuTe integral-constant wrapper returned by `cute::size(...)` directly as the non-type template argument to `cute::make_int_sequence<N>`:

```cpp
cute::for_each(
    cute::make_int_sequence<cute::size(epi)>{},
    auto i { epi(i) = ElementOutput(accum(i)); });

cute::for_each(
    cute::make_int_sequence<cute::size(scale)>{},
    auto i { scale(i) = tXrSFA(i) * tXrSFB(0); });
```

The failure occurs when the object passed to `cute::size(...)` is a dependent function parameter or local object inside the surrounding template context.

### Problem

`cute::size(object)` returns a class-type integral-constant wrapper such as `cute::C<N>`. The wrapper provides a static `value` member and a constant conversion operator.

`cute::make_int_sequence<N>` ultimately forms an integer sequence whose non-type template argument must be a valid converted constant expression of the expected integral type.

In a dependent-template context, NVCC does not accept `cute::size(object)` directly as that template argument because the expression syntactically depends on the function parameter or local object.

NVCC reports:

```text
error: expression must have a constant value
note #2689-D: the value of parameter "obj" cannot be used as a constant
```

The same expression compiles in a non-dependent context, isolating the reproduced failure to dependent-template constant-expression evaluation.

### Reproduction

Minimal dependent-template reproduction:

```cpp
#include <cute/tensor.hpp>
#include <cute/numeric/integer_sequence.hpp>

using namespace cute;

template <class Tensor>
__host__ __device__ void use_seq(Tensor const& obj) {
  cute::for_each(
      cute::make_int_sequence<cute::size(obj)>{},
      auto i { (void)obj(i); });
}

__global__ void launcher() {
  auto frag = cute::make_fragment_like<float>(
      cute::make_shape(cute::Int<8>{}, cute::Int<4>{}));
  use_seq(frag);
}
```

Portable compile command:

```console
nvcc -c -std=c++20 original_dep.cu -o original_dep.obj \
  --gpu-architecture=sm_89 \
  --expt-relaxed-constexpr \
  --expt-extended-lambda \
  -I<PATH_TO_CUTLASS>/include \
  -I<PATH_TO_CUDA>/include
```

The include paths should point to the CUTLASS/CuTe and CUDA installations being tested.

The reproduction used:

```text
CUDA/NVCC 13.2
CUTLASS revision e6e2cc29
C++20
SM89 compilation target
MSVC as the NVCC host compiler
```

The original dependent form failed consistently in two attempts:

```text
return code: 1

original_dep.cu(10): error: expression must have a constant value
    cute::for_each(cute::make_int_sequence<cute::size(obj)>{},
                                           ^

original_dep.cu(10): note #2689-D: the value of parameter "obj" (declared at line 9) cannot be used as a constant
    cute::for_each(cute::make_int_sequence<cute::size(obj)>{},
                                                      ^

detected during instantiation of:
void use_seq(const Tensor&) [
  with Tensor=cute::Tensor<
      cute::ArrayEngine<float, 32ULL>,
      cute::Layout<
          cute::tuple<cute::_8, cute::_4>,
          cute::tuple<cute::_1, cute::_8>>>
]

1 error detected in the compilation of original_dep.cu.
```

Controlled results:

```text
ORIGINAL non-dependent:
  cute::make_int_sequence<cute::size(object)>
  return code: 0

CORRECTED non-dependent:
  cute::make_int_sequence<decltype(cute::size(object))::value>
  return code: 0

CONTROL:
  cute::make_int_sequence<32>
  return code: 0

ORIGINAL dependent, attempt 1:
  cute::make_int_sequence<cute::size(object)>
  return code: 1

ORIGINAL dependent, attempt 2:
  cute::make_int_sequence<cute::size(object)>
  return code: 1

CORRECTED dependent:
  cute::make_int_sequence<decltype(cute::size(object))::value>
  return code: 0

Type-equivalence test:
  return code: 0
```

### Tested fix

Extract the static integral value from the type returned by `cute::size(...)`:

```cpp
decltype(cute::size(object))::value
```

`decltype` is unevaluated, and the resulting `::value` supplies the required compile-time integral value without evaluating the dependent function parameter or local object as part of the non-type template argument.

Exact production diff:

```diff
--- a/cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/cutlass_kernels/fp8_blockscale_gemm/ada_blockwise_gemm/sm89_fp8_gemm_1d1d.cuh
+++ b/cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/cutlass_kernels/fp8_blockscale_gemm/ada_blockwise_gemm/sm89_fp8_gemm_1d1d.cuh
@@ -124,7 +124,7 @@
-    cute::for_each(cute::make_int_sequence<cute::size(epi)>{},
+    cute::for_each(cute::make_int_sequence<decltype(cute::size(epi))::value>{},
                    auto i { epi(i) = ElementOutput(accum(i)); });
@@ -377,7 +377,7 @@
-          cute::for_each(cute::make_int_sequence<cute::size(scale)>{},
+          cute::for_each(cute::make_int_sequence<decltype(cute::size(scale))::value>{},
                          auto i { scale(i) = tXrSFA(i) * tXrSFB(0); });
@@ -408,7 +408,7 @@
-          cute::for_each(cute::make_int_sequence<cute::size(scale)>{},
+          cute::for_each(cute::make_int_sequence<decltype(cute::size(scale))::value>{},
                          auto i { scale(i) = tXrSFA(i) * tXrSFB(0); });
@@ -426,7 +426,7 @@
-        cute::for_each(cute::make_int_sequence<cute::size(scale)>{},
+        cute::for_each(cute::make_int_sequence<decltype(cute::size(scale))::value>{},
                        auto i { scale(i) = tXrSFA(i) * tXrSFB(0); });
```

The corrected dependent form compiles successfully:

```text
return code: 0
```

A compile-time equivalence test confirms that the original non-dependent form, the corrected form, and the built-in control produce the same type:

```cpp
cute::make_int_sequence<cute::size(object)>

cute::make_int_sequence<
    decltype(cute::size(object))::value>

cute::make_int_sequence<32>
```

For the tested shape, all three resolve to the same integer sequence:

```text
integer_sequence<int, 0, 1, ..., 31>
```


### Expected behavior

-

### actual behavior

.

### additional notes

-

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and checked the [documentation](https://nvidia.github.io/TensorRT-LLM/) and [examples](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/examples) for answers to frequently asked questions.

items.title: [None][fix] MoE: keep separate NVFP4 gate/up global scales where supported
items.body:
## Description

An NVFP4 checkpoint may store a different `weight_scale_2` for the gate (`w1`) and up (`w3`) projections of the same expert. The MoE weight loader reconciled the pair with `max()` and warned, which silently costs accuracy on whichever projection has the smaller scale.

The trtllm-gen FC1 kernel does not need that reconcile: it takes the two global scales as separate scalars (`output1_scale_gate_scalar` for the gate half, `output1_scale_scalar` for the gated intermediate), so such a checkpoint can be reproduced exactly.

- `NVFP4FusedMoEMethod.supports_split_gate_up_weight_scale_2` (False by default, True on `NVFP4TRTLLMGenFusedMoEBaseMethod`) says whether the backend's kernel can consume both.
- The gate/up pair now goes through one helper, `_resolve_gate_up_weight_scale_2`. Single-alpha backends (Cutlass) keep the old `max()` behaviour and its warning; split-scale backends get both values back untouched.
- `_reconcile_and_compute_alphas` takes an optional `dst_fc31_up_alpha` and writes the up half's alpha there.
- `fc31_scale_c` rescales the *gated intermediate* before the GEMM2 input quantization, so on trtllm-gen it is derived from the up-half alpha while `fc31_alpha` keeps the gate half. The shared-expert host copy consumed by online EPLB uses the same formula, so a migrated expert lands on the same value as a main slot.

Nothing changes when the two halves agree: the up alpha then equals `fc31_alpha`, and the staging tensor is dropped as soon as `fc31_scale_c` has been computed.

## Test Coverage

`tests/unittest/_torch/moe/test_moe_nvfp4_gate_up_scale2.py` — new CPU-only unit tests over the loader's alpha bookkeeping with small synthetic scale tensors:

- equal gate/up scales give the same single alpha on both backend kinds;
- unequal scales on a split-capable backend keep the gate scale in `fc31_alpha` and the up scale in the separate up alpha, with no reconcile;
- `fc31_scale_c` on the trtllm-gen method comes from the up column, and the staging tensor is dropped afterwards;
- a backend without split support falls back to `max()` and warns exactly once.

- Test cases are provided for new code paths (see [test instructions](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/tests#1-how-does-the-ci-work))

items.title: [None][fix] Re-resolve the MoE op provider once the per-layer quant config is known
items.body:
## Description

`TRTLLMGenFusedMoE` resolves its op provider (native TRTLLM-Gen or FlashInfer)
in `__init__`, but `ConfigurableMoE` installs the final per-layer quant config
on the backend only just before calling `create_weights()`. With layerwise
quantization a checkpoint can declare NVFP4 at model level while leaving
individual MoE layers unquantized: at `__init__` time such a layer still looks
quantized, so it keeps the native provider. Only FlashInfer implements the BF16
MoE kernels, so the layer then fails in `run_bf16_moe` at warmup.

The provider selection moves into `_select_op_provider()`, which is now called
twice: once in `__init__` and again at the top of `create_weights()`, before
the quant method is resolved. Both reads then come from the same config, so the
provider and `_get_quant_method()` cannot disagree.

`ConfigurableMoE` keeps a `use_flashinfer` mirror that feeds
communication-strategy selection, so `create_weights()` refreshes it after the
backend returns. Only the mirror is refreshed. Rebuilding the strategy there
would run a collective in the middle of per-layer weight creation (the NVLink
strategies allocate MNNVL memory, and `destroy()` is collective as well), which
deadlocks every rank. Provider and strategy can only actually disagree for the
NVLink two-sided pair, and that combination is rejected with
`NotImplementedError` rather than repaired silently: picking the wrong alltoall
kernel would be a numerical error rather than a crash, and the communication
method can be chosen explicitly for such a model instead.

## Test Coverage

New CPU-only unit test `tests/unittest/_torch/moe/test_moe_op_provider_resync.py`:

- a layer that starts from a model-level NVFP4 config and ends up with a BF16
  per-layer config moves from the native provider to FlashInfer in
  `create_weights()`;
- a layer whose quant config is unchanged keeps its original provider;
- a BF16 layer stays on the native provider when the FlashInfer BF16 kernels
  are unavailable;
- `ConfigurableMoE.create_weights()` mirrors a provider switch, leaves the
  mirror and `comm` alone when there is no switch, and raises
  `NotImplementedError` for both NVLink two-sided strategies.

Heavy pieces (quant methods, op-backend construction, communication strategies)
are stubbed, so the tests need no GPU.

## PR Checklist

items.title: [None][fix] Re-plan FlashInfer decode schedule on page-table changes under CUDA graphs
items.body:
## Description

With CUDA graphs enabled, the FlashInfer decode kernel runs the split-KV tile schedule that `plan()` computed: the request/kv-tile index lists and `kv_chunk_size` live in the wrapper's persistent plan workspace, and graph replay never re-enters `forward_impl`. Whatever plan was captured is what every replay executes, so the plan has to be kept current from `prepare()`.

`_refresh_fa2_cuda_graph_plans()` already does that, keyed on a page tuple (`fa2_plan_num_blocks`) recorded when the decode plan ran. The recording was gated on the wrapper being both a graph tensor-core wrapper (`head_dim > 128`) *and* labelled `'fa2'`. Any decode wrapper outside that case never got a tuple, so the refresh skipped it.

That is invisible for a model with a single decode wrapper, because `prepare()` plans it eagerly. It is not invisible for a model with more than one decode wrapper — a mixed sliding-window/full-attention checkpoint has one wrapper per distinct window — because `prepare()` defers multi-wrapper plans to `forward_impl`, which graph replay never reaches. Every replay then reused the plan captured for the warmup batch: one `max_seq_len` dummy in generation slot 0 and one-token dummies elsewhere. Slot 0 kept full KV coverage, so batch size 1 looked fine, but every other slot attended only its first `kv_chunk_size` tokens and never its own output, and batched decode degenerated into repetition. The TRTLLM attention backend was unaffected.

The fix records the page tuple for every non-`trtllm-gen` decode wrapper whenever the metadata is graph-captured, so the refresh re-plans all of them when the generation page counts change. `trtllm-gen` stays excluded because it already refreshes its own block tables and KV lengths per step in `prepare()`; the eager path is unchanged, since `is_cuda_graph` is false there and `forward_impl` re-plans anyway. The plan and its stream sync still run only on a page-count change, so this costs nothing on steps where the page table is stable.

The recording rule moves into a small module-level helper (`_records_fa2_plan`) rather than staying an inline condition, so the part that regressed is directly unit-testable without a device — the surrounding `decode_plan()` closure needs FlashInfer and real KV buffers.

## Test Coverage

New CPU-only unit test: `tests/unittest/_torch/attention/test_flashinfer_plan_refresh.py`

- `test_every_non_trtllm_gen_decode_plan_is_recorded_under_graphs` / `test_trtllm_gen_is_not_recorded` / `test_eager_plans_are_not_recorded` cover the recording rule, including the wrapper class that regressed (graph-captured, backend resolved to `'auto'`, no tensor-core wrapper) which the old condition dropped.
- `test_page_table_change_replans_every_recorded_wrapper` covers the multi-wrapper case: two plan-params entries both carrying a page tuple must both be re-planned when the generation page counts change.
- `test_an_unchanged_page_table_does_not_replan` and `test_no_generations_clears_the_recorded_page_tuple` pin the two no-op paths.

End-to-end, the change was validated on a mixed sliding-window/full-attention MoE checkpoint on 4 GPUs (TP4/EP4) with CUDA graphs and the overlap scheduler: a 16-example GSM8K canary goes from 18.8 to 87.5 and a 100-example set from 7.0 to 95.0, matching the reference implementation. A fully cached-prefix decode reproducer that produced non-finite logits at the first decode step on 10/10 runs now produces none. Eager (no-graph) results are unchanged.

## PR Checklist

Please review the following before submitting your PR:
- PR description clearly explains what and why. If using CodeRabbit's summary, please make sure it makes sense.
- PR Follows [TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of your knowledge.
- Test cases are provided for new code paths (see [test instructions](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/tests#1-how-does-the-ci-work))
- If PR introduces API changes, an appropriate PR label is added - either `api-compatible` or `api-breaking`. For `api-breaking`, include `BREAKING` in the PR title.
- Any new dependencies have been scanned for license and vulnerabilities
- [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) updated if ownership changes
- Documentation updated as needed

items.title: [None][fix] Make llm_args use the canonical custom-tokenizer alias table

labels.name: api-compatible
labels.description: Accepted LLM API contract change that is backwards-compatible

items.body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- `llm_args.py` now uses the canonical `TOKENIZER_ALIASES` table.
- This removes alias-table drift and preserves existing tokenizer resolution behavior.
- The change does not add an import cycle or alter public declarations.
- Error handling remains appropriate for invalid tokenizer identifiers.
- No configuration files or test-list files changed.

## QA Engineer Review

- Added seven CPU-only tests in `tests/unittest/llmapi/test_tokenizer_aliases.py`.
- The tests cover:
  - Canonical alias-table identity.
  - Alias module and class-path validity.
  - Alias resolution through `TorchLlmArgs`.
  - Full import-path resolution.
  - Rejection of invalid identifiers.
- No matching entry exists in `tests/integration/test_lists/`.
- The tests are suitable for unit-test discovery and isolate imports and downloads with stubs.
- Verdict: sufficient.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Description

The built-in `--custom_tokenizer` aliases live in `tensorrt_llm/tokenizer/tokenizer.py` as `TOKENIZER_ALIASES`, and `load_custom_tokenizer`, `trtllm-bench` (`tensorrt_llm/bench/utils/data.py`) and the serve benchmark scripts (`tensorrt_llm/serve/scripts/backend_request_func.py`) all resolve against that table.

`tensorrt_llm/llmapi/llm_args.py` did not. It carried a second, hand-maintained copy of the dict, used by the `TorchLlmArgs` tokenizer validator. Aliases added to the canonical table were never mirrored into the copy, so the two diverged. For a missing alias the validator's

```python
tokenizer_path = TOKENIZER_ALIASES.get(self.custom_tokenizer, self.custom_tokenizer)
```

falls back to the bare alias, which then hits `tokenizer_path.rsplit('.', 1)` with nothing to split on and raises

```
Failed to load custom tokenizer '<alias>': not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1).
Expected format: 'module.path.ClassName' or a recognized alias.
```

The failure mode is confusing because the same alias string works everywhere else, and the error text points at the identifier's format rather than at the missing registration.

This PR deletes the duplicate and imports the canonical table, so all four resolution sites share one definition and a newly registered alias is reachable from every entry point at once.

On the import: `tensorrt_llm.tokenizer` does not import `tensorrt_llm.llmapi`, so this adds no cycle, and `llm_args` already imports the same package indirectly through the `tensorrt_llm.llmapi.tokenizer` compatibility shim a few lines below.

No behavior change beyond the alias set: the resolution logic, the error message, and the accepted `module.path.ClassName` form are untouched.

## Test Coverage

New CPU-only unit tests in `tests/unittest/llmapi/test_tokenizer_aliases.py`:

* `test_llm_args_reuses_the_tokenizer_package_alias_table` — asserts `llm_args.TOKENIZER_ALIASES` *is* `tensorrt_llm.tokenizer.TOKENIZER_ALIASES`, i.e. an object identity check that a re-introduced copy would fail.
* `test_every_alias_maps_to_a_module_and_a_class` — every registered value splits into a non-empty module part and class part, which is the invariant the `rsplit` depends on.
* `test_alias_resolves_through_llm_args` — parametrized over every alias key, constructs `TorchLlmArgs(model="dummy", custom_tokenizer=<alias>)` and checks the tokenizer that comes back was loaded from the alias's exact module and class. Each aliased tokenizer module is shadowed with a stub in `sys.modules` for the duration of the test (`importlib.import_module` returns a `sys.modules` hit without touching the filesystem), so the resolution path runs end to end with no real tokenizer imports and no downloads. This is the case that regressed.
* `test_full_import_path_still_works` and `test_unknown_identifier_without_a_module_part_is_rejected` — the two non-alias inputs, so the fix does not widen what is accepted.

Status: `pytest tests/unittest/llmapi/test_tokenizer_aliases.py` was run against a built checkout and passes — 7 passed. No GPU is required.

items.title: [None][infra] Skip pre-merge perf gating when main has already regressed and refactor the pre-merge perf-sanity list
items.body:
## Description

Two coupled changes to the pre-merge perf-sanity gate. They are in one PR because
either alone is worse than neither: part 2 enables gating on 13 cases, 3 of which are
regressed on `main` right now, and part 1 is what stops those from blocking every PR
on day one.

### Part 1 — do not fail a pre-merge perf case when `main` has already regressed

Both perf pipelines compare against the same post-merge baseline. Post-merge runs
daily on the `main` tip and the baseline is derived from that history; pre-merge runs
on a PR branch and compares against it. So once a regression lands on `main`, every PR
measures the same regressed value and every PR fails a perf-sanity test it did not
break — blocking the whole queue until someone lands a fix, after which everyone else
must rebase.

The new rule:

- If the latest post-merge value for a test case misses its baseline by more than the
  **pre-merge** threshold (10%), **do not** evaluate whether the pre-merge result is
  regressive. As long as the functional test passes, the perf test is treated as
  passed.
- If the latest post-merge value is within the pre-merge threshold, evaluate the
  pre-merge result.
- That evaluation compares the pre-merge value against the post-merge baseline
  (unchanged).
- If the pre-merge result is regressive, fail that test case.

`prepare_regressive_test_cases` now returns the set of exempt `cmd_idx` and
`check_perf_regression` takes it as an optional kwarg, warning on exempt cases but
excluding them from the raised error. The "latest post-merge value" is
`latest_history_data_dict`, which `get_history_data` already fetches and
`prepare_regressive_test_cases` already receives, so **no new OpenSearch query** is
issued. Both functions have exactly one call site each, in the same file.

Three design points, deliberate rather than accidental:

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Which threshold decides "post-merge is regressive" | The **pre-merge** threshold (10%). The latest post-merge *value* is re-evaluated against the same baseline via a shared `_is_regressive` helper; the `b_is_regression` the post-merge run recorded is **not** reused, because it was computed at the tighter 5% post-merge bar. |
| Granularity | The **whole test case** (`cmd_idx`), not the individual metric. |
| What is recorded | **No new field.** The pre-merge document's `b_is_regression` is uploaded exactly as measured; only the `RuntimeError` is suppressed. |

Consequences a reviewer should weigh, documented in both READMEs rather than papered
over:

- **The exemption is exactly as wide as the failure it prevents, and no wider.** This
  is why the threshold is re-evaluated instead of reused. A case sitting 6% below
  baseline is *not* exempt: a PR reproducing that value never fails the 10% gate, so
  there was nothing to exempt — and a PR that takes the same case to 20% down still
  fails. The blind window is `≥10% down`, precisely the band where the gate would have
  fired on `main`'s own value anyway.
- **Inside that window the case is exempt entirely.** A further regression the PR adds
  on top of `main`'s still passes. That is inherent to exempting a whole test case; the
  alternative — comparing pre-merge against the latest post-merge *value* rather than
  the baseline — is a noisier design and was not adopted.
- **A broken post-merge record does not disarm the gate.** Metric absent, null,
  non-numeric, zero and negative all fail to exempt, by construction rather than by
  luck.
- **It self-clears, and that hides the regression.** Nothing seeds `d_baseline_*`, so
  the effective baseline is the rolling P95/P5 window in `calculate_baseline_metrics`.
  Within days the baseline drifts down, the latest post-merge value comes back inside
  the threshold, and the gate re-arms — against the *lowered* bar if nobody landed a
  fix.
- **One flaky post-merge point disarms the gate for a whole post-merge cycle.**
  "Latest" has no smoothing.
- **The escape hatch is manual:** mark the offending post-merge document
  `b_is_valid: false` in OpenSearch so the history query drops it.
- **The exempting document may come from a different stage.** `s_stage_name` is not a
  match key, so "latest" is whichever stage ran last.
- `test_visual_gen_perf_sanity.py` inherits this (it passes no `fail_on_regression`);
  `host_perf/regression_helper.py` passes `False` and is inert either way.

### Part 2 — refactor the pre-merge case list

3 of the current 5 pre-merge stages carry `FUNCTIONAL-ONLY` in the stage name, which
`test_perf_sanity.py` reads as a substring to set `fail_on_regression = False` — so a
perf regression on those stages cannot fail CI at all. Two of the three run `e2e`
cases.

Replaced with 13 disagg `ctx_only` / `gen_only` cases that all gate on perf. No 1k1k.
Per model 2 `ctx_only` (small + large concurrency, small = `con1` where a config
exists) plus 1 `gen_only`; DeepSeek-V4-Pro gets 2 `gen_only`. Qwen on GB200;
DeepSeek-R1, GLM-5, DeepSeek-V4-Pro on GB300.

| # | Model / GPU | Mode | Config stem (`…_ccb-NIXL`) | GPUs / nodes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Qwen3-235B / GB200 | ctx_only | `gb200_qwen3-235b-fp4_8k1k_con1_ctx1_tp1_gen1_tep4_eplb0_mtp0` | 4 / 1 |
| 2 | Qwen3-235B / GB200 | ctx_only | `gb200_qwen3-235b-fp4_8k1k_con1024_ctx1_tp1_gen1_dep8_eplb0_mtp0` | 4 / 1 |
| 3 | Qwen3-235B / GB200 | gen_only | `gb200_qwen3-235b-fp4_8k1k_con1_ctx1_tp1_gen1_tep4_eplb0_mtp0` | 8 / 2 |
| 4 | DeepSeek-R1 / GB300 | ctx_only | `gb300_deepseek-r1-fp4_8k1k_con1_ctx1_dep4_gen1_tep8_eplb0_mtp3` | 4 / 1 |
| 5 | DeepSeek-R1 / GB300 | ctx_only | `gb300_deepseek-r1-fp4_8k1k_con4096_ctx1_dep4_gen1_dep16_eplb0_mtp1` | 4 / 1 |
| 6 | DeepSeek-R1 / GB300 | gen_only | `gb300_deepseek-r1-fp4_128k8k_con256_ctx1_pp4_gen1_dep8_eplb0_mtp1` | 12 / 3 |
| 7 | GLM-5 / GB300 | ctx_only | `gb300_glm-5-fp4_8k1k_con1_ctx1_dep2_gen1_tep8_eplb0_mtp3` | 4 / 1 |
| 8 | GLM-5 / GB300 | ctx_only | `gb300_glm-5-fp4_8k1k_con1024_ctx1_dep2_gen1_dep8_eplb256_mtp1` | 4 / 1 |
| 9 | GLM-5 / GB300 | gen_only | `gb300_glm-5-fp4_8k1k_con1024_ctx1_dep2_gen1_dep8_eplb256_mtp1` | 12 / 3 |
| 10 | DeepSeek-V4-Pro / GB300 | ctx_only | `gb300_deepseek-v4-pro-fp4_8k1k_con8_ctx1_dep4_gen4_tep8_eplb0_mtp3` | 4 / 1 |
| 11 | DeepSeek-V4-Pro / GB300 | ctx_only | `gb300_deepseek-v4-pro-fp4_8k1k_con666_ctx6_dep4_gen1_dep16_eplb384_mtp3` | 4 / 1 |
| 12 | DeepSeek-V4-Pro / GB300 | gen_only | `gb300_deepseek-v4-pro-fp4_8k1k_con8_ctx1_dep4_gen4_tep8_eplb0_mtp3` | 36 / 9 |
| 13 | DeepSeek-V4-Pro / GB300 | gen_only | `gb300_deepseek-v4-pro-fp4_8k1k_con666_ctx6_dep4_gen1_dep16_eplb384_mtp3` | 40 / 10 |

The `gen_only` picks collectively cover small concurrency (#3), large concurrency
(#9), PP and 128k ISL (#6, `ctx1_pp4`), and MTP (#6/#9 mtp1, #4/#7 mtp3), at the
smallest node count available per model. All 8 `ctx_only` cases fit a single 4-GPU
node — `submit.py` sizes `ctx_only` from `worker_config.ctx` with exactly one server,
ignoring `num_ctx_servers`.

Dropping `FUNCTIONAL-ONLY` from the two surviving stage names is the entire mechanism
that turns them into gating stages.

Five things worth calling out explicitly:

1. **#10 and #12 are actively waived** (`waives.txt`, `https://nvbugs/6668776` for the
   V4 `con8` ctx_only and `https://nvbugs/6661856` for its gen_only sibling — this is
   also the real reason V4 `con8` gen_only data has been dark since 2026-08-10). Both
   are enrolled in the test-db so they activate when the waives lift, but **#12 gets
   no pre-merge Jenkins stage yet**: it would allocate 36 GPUs on 9 nodes per PR just
   to run a skip. There is a Groovy comment at that stage citing the nvbug. #10 does
   get a stage — it costs a quarter of a node.
2. **#4 was an orphan** — its config existed but the id appeared in no test list and no
   waive. It is added to the GB300 **post_merge** block too; without a post-merge
   baseline its pre-merge gate would be a silent no-op.
3. **Three picks are regressed on `main` right now** (#7 −36.3%, #8 −22.3%, #5 −8.8%,
   one unbroken episode since 2026-08-28, still flagging 09-05). Part 1 makes them
   auto-exempt rather than PR-blocking; they begin gating when `main` recovers. This is
   the intended interaction, but it does mean 3 of the 13 gates are dormant at merge.
4. **Deviation from a pure deletion on B200.** `l0_b200_multi_nodes_perf_sanity_ctx1_node1_gpu4_gen1_node1_gpu8.yml`
   had a pre_merge block holding only the dsr1 `con1536` gen_only case, and B200 is not
   in the model→GPU mapping — but no other list carried that config, so deleting the
   block would orphan it. It moves into the post_merge block instead, and that stage
   goes from 2 splits to 3, because `gen_only` requires exactly one test per split
   (`submit.py` `select_test_case_line` raises on zero *or* many).
5. **The new list has no track record as a gate.** All 7 currently-gating cases leave
   the pre-merge list, which removes the suite's only long gating history (1.18% flag
   rate, 308 of 26,172 records over 3 months). Every new case has post-merge history,
   but none has been exercised as a PR-blocking gate.

Declared pre-merge perf-sanity cost:

| | Stages | Nodes | GPUs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Today | 5 | 9 | 44 |
| After this PR | 7 | 21 | 84 |
| + V4 `con8` when its waive lifts | +1 | +9 | +36 |

## Test Coverage

`tests/unittest/others/test_perf_regression_branch.py` — 9 tests → 48, covering the
exemption firing (Tier-A `d_baseline_*` and Tier-B rolling-baseline paths), every way
it must **not** fire (`cmd_idx` absent, mapped to `None`, metric absent, null,
non-numeric, zero, negative, exactly at the threshold, and — the row that separates
this design from the earlier one — regressed on `main` but still *within* the 10%
gate), that a record carrying only a `b_is_regression: True` verdict and no value does
not exempt, minimize as well as maximize metrics, per-`cmd_idx` keying with a 2-case
mix of exempt and non-exempt, and inertness on post-merge runs, under
`fail_on_regression=False`, and when the history query itself failed (no `TypeError`).
Every "does not raise" row is paired with a structurally identical "raises" row
differing only in the history fake, so a degenerate always-true or always-false
predicate turns half the matrix red.

The module also gains the `pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_only` it was missing. Without
it, `tests/unittest/conftest.py`'s `pytest_ignore_collect` dropped the whole file from
the only stage that collects `unittest/others`, so **none of the pre-existing 9 tests
ran anywhere**.

Verification performed:

- 48/48 pass with the change. Run against a 5%-verdict-reuse implementation of the same
  feature, the file fails exactly 7 and passes 41: the 5 cases where the exemption should
  now fire but the old code required a recorded `b_is_regression: True`, plus
  `verdict-without-a-value` — the discriminator, since the old code exempts on a bare
  verdict and therefore does not raise — and the no-new-field check. Positive controls
  in that run prove a regression really does raise today. Sibling suite
  `tests/unittest/tools/test_perf_sanity_matching.py`: 19 passed.
- `scripts/check_test_list.py --validate` → rc=0, 1966 unique test entries validated;
  `--check-duplicate-waives` → rc=0. (Both must be run with Python ≥3.10; the hook's
  `python3` shebang resolves to 3.6 on some dev boxes and the script then dies in its
  own type annotations.)
- For each of the 5 `gen_only` stages, `jenkins/scripts/perf/submit.py` emits a launch
  script rather than raising `ValueError`, with derived sizing matching every declared
  `gpuCount`/`nodeCount`: qwen 8/2, glm-5 12/3, dsr1 12/3, V4 `con666` 40/10, V4
  `con8` 36/9.
- No `FUNCTIONAL-ONLY` stage name remains; every test-db context key equals its
  filename stem; all 13 config YAMLs exist under
  `tests/scripts/perf-sanity/disaggregated/`.
- `pre-commit` clean on all changed files (`ruff`, `ruff-format`, `codespell`,
  whitespace, yaml, legacy-lint-config verify).

Post-merge follow-up after this lands: confirm #4 starts uploading (it was an orphan),
confirm #6 resumes uploading (last upload 2026-07-23 while its sibling from the same
YAML is current), then confirm the 3 currently-exempt cases begin gating once `main`
recovers.

## PR Checklist

Please review the following before submitting your PR:
- PR description clearly explains what and why. If using CodeRabbit's summary, please make sure it makes sense.
- PR Follows [TRT-LLM CODING GUIDELINES](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/CODING_GUIDELINES.md) to the best of your knowledge.
